anchor.quote: Write $m$ for an item's position in tape order.
Write $u$ for the number of bits in one address field.
Write $V$ for the stored bit volume, the total number of bits the array holds.

anchor.note: Asymptotic notation covered by big-O notation and asymptotic analysis in the reader profile.
Logarithms, covered by the known concept of logarithms and floor/ceiling (lg, log base 2).

gaps.term: Padded array size and coefficient width
gaps.quote: the padded array holds $\Theta(n/\log n)$ entries, so $V=\Theta(n)$ (cited)
gaps.note: The page does not say how the padding is chosen, so the reader cannot check why the padded array has Theta(n/log n) entries or why each coefficient has Theta(log n) bits. The conclusion V = Theta(n) therefore rests on unexplained sizes.

gaps.quote: Scanning all $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of the $\Theta(\log n)$ levels costs $\Theta(n\log n)$ (cited).
gaps.note: The page never relates the number of levels to the array length or the number of address bits, so the reader cannot check why there are Theta(log n) levels. The Theta(n log n) cost follows only from that unexplained count.

gaps.term: Pairing of entries at each level
gaps.quote: A level pairs entries whose addresses differ in one bit, and successive levels pair different bits.
gaps.note: This is stated as a property of the transform's levels, but the page does not give the index structure of the transform that produces it. The reader, who has not studied the FFT literature, cannot check why butterflies pair addresses that differ in one bit or why successive levels use different bits.
